ColorDistance enum

Distance-metric strategy for nearest-color matching.

Cases: Euclidean · Cie76 · Cie94 · Cie2000

PHP also provides cases(), from() and tryFrom().

MethodSummary
between(Color $a, Color $b): floatDistance between two colors under this metric.
betweenLab(array $labA, array $labB): floatDistance between pre-computed Lab triples — the hot-loop entry point, letting callers amortize the sRGB -> Lab conversion over a memoized palette. EUCLIDEAN is an RGB-space metric with no meaning here: it throws instead of silently substituting Lab-space magnitudes, so mixing the two scales fails loudly.

ColorMath final class

Perceptual color-space conversion math: sRGB -> linear -> CIE XYZ (D65) -> CIE L*a*b*.

MethodSummary

static rgbToXyz(int $r, int $g, int $b): arrayConvert an sRGB byte triplet to CIE XYZ (D65), Y normalized to 0-1.
static srgbToLinear(int $byte): floatInverse-compatibility (gamma) decode one sRGB byte to linear light 0-1.
static linearToXyz(float $r, float $g, float $b): arrayApply the IEC 61966-2-1 sRGB -> CIE XYZ (D65) matrix to linear light.
static xyzToLab(array $xyz): arrayConvert CIE XYZ (D65) to CIE L*a*b* (CIE 1976).

ColorProfile enum

Terminal color capability profile — THE single vocabulary.

Cases: TrueColor · Ansi256 · Ansi240 · Ansi · Ansi8 · Fgbg · Ascii · NoTTY

PHP also provides cases(), from() and tryFrom().

MethodSummary
static fromColorProfile(self $p): self
static fromCore(\SugarCraft\Core\Util\ColorProfile $core): selfLift a sugar-core Util\ColorProfile onto this vocabulary (CP-22).
toCore(): \SugarCraft\Core\Util\ColorProfileProject onto the five-rung Core enum (CP-22). Lossy on purpose: Core has no 240/8/fgbg rungs, so each lands on the nearest rung that never emits a color the profile could not render — Ansi240 to Ansi256, Ansi8 to Ansi, Fgbg to Ascii.
label(): stringHuman-readable label for display.
description(): stringShort description for display.
maxColors(): intMaximum colors this profile supports.
degradedTo(): ?selfWalk the profile downgrade chain to the next simpler profile. Returns null when already at the simplest (NoTTY). The walk is about emission richness, not provenance: standing on either colorless rung it cannot tell an operator opt-out from absent hardware — DetectionChain::userOptedOut() answers that (CP-20).
allowsColor(): boolWhether this profile permits ANSI COLOR rendering.

DetectionChain final class

Shared terminal color detection chain — the single source of truth for environment-based color capability detection.

MethodSummary
static detect(array $env = []): selfRun the detection chain on an environment array.
level(): stringGet the detected level as a string.
source(): stringGet the source of the detection result.
term(): stringGet the TERM value used in detection. Values at or below self::TERM_MAX_BYTES come back byte-identical; a longer value is clamped to the ceiling here rather than exported raw — the accessor is where TERM leaves the chain, and detection itself already matched it by equality before any consumer could see it.
allowsColor(): boolWhether the ladder answered on a rung that renders color at all.
isForced(): boolTrue when the answer came from an explicit force leg rather than a capability read or a suppression. Callers gating on TTY presence use this to yield: upstream parity is Detect() = isatty() || forced() (CP-07), so an operator who PINNED color through the force machinery keeps that rung even on a piped stream. Suppression legs are NOT force — NO_COLOR/CLICOLOR=0/TERM=dumb ask for less output, never for escape sequences past a pipe, so they keep the gate.
static userOptedOut(array $env = []): boolDid the OPERATOR opt out of color, as opposed to the hardware lacking a TTY? True iff a suppression leg (NO_COLOR, CLICOLOR=0, TERM=dumb) actually FIRED the answer. A force leg outranking a suppression reads FALSE here — the rung in force is not a suppression, whoever asked. This is the discriminator the profile enums deliberately do not carry: since CP-05 both stories answer colorless rungs (Ascii for the opt-out, NoTTY for absent hardware) and a name cannot hold two truths, while a CLI repairing its own defaults (--color=always) or drawing a doctor panel needs the WHY (CP-20, sugar-colorprofile-023; the full enum split is reserved for 2.0 — decision candidate #4).
toProfile(): ColorProfileConvert the detection level to the profile enum.
toColorProfile(): ColorProfileConvert the detection level to a ColorProfile enum.

Env final class

Single environment-resolution rule shared by every detection surface.

MethodSummary
static resolve(array $injected): arrayResolve the effective environment map for one detection run.
static value(array $resolved, string $key): ?stringRead one variable from a resolved map, normalizing absent/false/null to null.
static isForceValue(?string $value): boolThe force-value grammar shared by every CLICOLOR_FORCE reader: a value forces when it is SET and is neither the empty string nor the exact falsy spelling '0' — the termenv/chafa rule ("any non-empty != 0"), which the README's chalk-escape-hatch justification invokes while the old literal '1'-only reading silently stripped color for the CLICOLOR_FORCE=true|yes|on|2 spellings real dotfiles and CI images export. Only '0' and unset/empty are falsy; every other non-empty string forces. Env owns this single rule so the three readers — DetectionChain step 1, TerminalProbe's capability mapping and Probe::isForceColor — cannot drift apart (XPLAT-02).
static sanitize(string $value): stringMake an untrusted environment value safe to interpolate into a source string: strip C0/C1/DEL control bytes (which could forge escape sequences downstream consumers print) and cap the length.

Probe final class

Static probe for terminal color profile and environment-based color detection.

MethodSummary
static colorProfile(): ColorProfileNegotiated color profile after walking every environment variable in the canonical precedence order, then the optional infocmp phase-2 upgrade.
static isNoColor(): boolNO_COLOR is set to a non-empty value. An empty string means UNSET per the no-color.org convention the whole ecosystem follows.
static isForceColor(): boolCLICOLOR_FORCE carries a force value — set, non-empty, and not exactly '0' (the termenv/chafa grammar owned by Env::isForceValue(), shared with DetectionChain step 1 and TerminalProbe) — forcing TrueColor regardless of other settings.
static reducedMotion(): boolReduced motion preference — checks REDUCE_MOTION then PREFERS_REDUCED_MOTION. Explicit negative spellings (0/false/no/off, case-insensitive) mean "not reduced"; any other non-empty value means reduced. The old polarity treated REDUCE_MOTION=false as TRUE, inverting the operator's declared preference.
static _reset(): void

InfocmpBinary final class

Single source of truth for locating the infocmp terminfo binary.

MethodSummary
static path(): ?stringAbsolute path to infocmp, or null when no roster candidate is a present AND executable file. The executable leg is what keeps this gate from drifting from sugar-image's ChafaBinary roster gate — see the class docblock's shared-rule note.
static runBounded(string $term, ?float $timeoutSeconds = null): ?stringThe ONE bounded infocmp execution surface, shared by every surface (synchronous Probe, the TerminalProbe phase-2 leg, and future callers). The pre-CP-11 shape carried two unbounded waits: the child was untimed (a wedged infocmp blocked the caller for its whole life) and its output was slurped without limit. Both arms are now bounded, and the answer is memoized per TERM so a per-tick consumer multiplies nothing.
static childEnvironment(?string $term = null): arrayThe environment every infocmp child receives, at every exec surface.
static isSafeTermName(string $term): boolIs $term shaped like a terminal name rather than an infocmp option?
